patients.summary: High school teacher who joins in 2022 healthy, is diagnosed with IBS by GI in late 2024 with situational anxiety around a job change, and after her last practice visit in December 2025 self-refers to endocrinology for a suspicious thyroid nodule that proves to be papillary carcinoma. Total thyroidectomy in April 2026 is complicated by postprocedural hypoparathyroidism; the practice hears of it late, through a pharmacy call, the patient and a delayed surgical letter.

documents.title: New Patient Inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to transfer primary care here; previous office in the Valley is cutting back hours and she wants easier access. Teaches high school, prefers summer or after 3:15 on school days. Membership info emailed. Booked new pt physical 8/17 at 9:00. Release of records form sent to her email, she will sign and send to her old office.

documents.title: New Patient Visit and Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Julie is a 42 y/o high school teacher establishing care. Coming from another primary care office; records release signed. Feels well. No complaints today, here mostly to have a doctor she can reach.

PMH: none ongoing.
PSH: C-section 2012, uncomplicated.
Meds: none.
Allergies: none to medications.
Family: father with hypertension. Mother has osteoporosis. A maternal aunt was treated for papillary thyroid cancer.
Social: teaches high school, lives in Amherst. Has never smoked. Does not drink. Walks most evenings when the weather allows.
Gyn: Pap with HPV co-test last year at her old office, she says normal. Mammogram last fall, normal per her.

ROS: negative across systems; sleeping fine, energy good, bowels regular.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no adenopathy, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, low transverse scar healed. Extremities without edema. Skin clear. Mood good.

Assessment / plan:
1. Adult health maintenance. Screening bloodwork today (CBC, CMP, lipids), plus one-time hep C and HIV screens which she agreed to.
2. Tdap today, last one she thinks was with her pregnancy.
3. Old records requested; will reconcile her Pap and mammogram dates when they arrive. Next mammogram due this fall, order placed.
4. Flu and COVID this fall at a nurse visit.
Follow-up: annual, or sooner by message.

events.reason: records from prior primary care office

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Eighteen pages arrived from her previous primary care office. Reviewed and abstracted:
- Cervical cytology with HPV co-test, June 2021: negative for intraepithelial lesion; HPV not detected. Repeat interval 5 years noted by that office.
- Bilateral screening mammogram, October 2021: no suspicious findings, BI-RADS 1.
- Problem list there: none active. History of cesarean delivery.
- Medications: none.
- Allergies: NKDA.
- Immunizations on file: COVID primary series spring 2021 plus booster, flu yearly.
Sent to PCP for sign-off.

documents.title: Your Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Julie, all of last week's bloodwork came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Your old records came in too and line up with what you told me. Nothing to do until your mammogram this fall.

documents.title: Vaccine Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came after school for vaccines. Afebrile, no current illness, no prior reactions. Influenza 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Bivalent COVID booster IM right deltoid. VIS reviewed. Observed 15 minutes, left feeling fine.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison with outside study of October 2021. The breasts are scattered fibroglandular density. No mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcification in either breast. Skin and nipples unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: No mammographic evidence of malignancy. BI-RADS 1, negative. Annual screening recommended.

documents.title: Mammogram
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your mammogram from last week was normal. Next one in about a year; I'll put the order in at your physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam before the school year starts. Doing well. Summer was quiet, lots of walking. No new symptoms; sleeping and eating normally, bowels regular. Still on no daily medicines.

PHQ-2 negative.

Exam: vitals as recorded, weight unchanged from last year. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen benign. No edema. Skin without concerning lesions.

Plan: CBC and CMP this morning. Mammogram due again in the fall, order in. Pap/HPV next due 2026. Colon cancer screening starts at 45, next year. Flu and the new COVID shot when the fall supply comes in. See her next summer.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count and chemistry panel are normal. Have a good start to the year.

documents.title: RE: Lab Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks! First week with students is Tuesday, wish me luck.

documents.title: Vaccine Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu IM L arm and 2023-24 COVID IM R arm. Feeling well today, temp normal. Tolerated both. Out after 15 min.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with November 2022. Scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No new mass, distortion or suspicious calcifications. Axillary regions unremarkable.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit. She turns 45 next month. Says she is fine, a bit tired from summer curriculum work but nothing she wants looked into. No meds.

Screens: PHQ-2 zero.

Exam: BP and weight in her usual range. Neck without nodes. Lungs clear, heart regular without murmur. Abdomen soft, no masses. No edema. Normal affect.

Plan:
- Colorectal screening is due at 45. We talked through colonoscopy vs stool testing; she prefers the FIT. Kit handed to her, to do after her birthday.
- Lipids and CMP today.
- Mammogram order renewed for winter.
- Vaccines in October.

documents.title: Cholesterol and Chemistry
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cholesterol numbers are in a good range and the chemistry panel is normal. Recheck lipids in a year or two.

documents.title: FIT Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Stool FIT negative. Portal note sent: repeat the kit in one year.

documents.title: Vaccine Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (2024-25) left deltoid, COVID 2024-25 right deltoid. Well today. Mentions she has felt run down for a few months; advised to book a visit with the doctor for that rather than wait for her physical. She will.

orders.reason: bloating and alternating bowel habit with fatigue

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Since roughly June she has been dragging. Tired by midafternoon, foggy, hard to keep up with grading. Belly bloats on and off, worse later in the day. Bowels have gone irregular: a few days constipated, then loose for a day or two, back and forth. No blood, no black stool. Weight steady, eating okay. No fevers. Periods regular. Took on more at work this year and admits it has been stressful.

O: Vitals as charted, afebrile. Looks tired but well. Thyroid not enlarged, no nodes. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, not distended, nontender today, normal bowel sounds, no masses or organomegaly.

A/P: Fatigue with bloating and alternating bowel habit, ~5 months. No alarm features and FIT was negative in September. Checking CBC with diff, CMP, TSH, ferritin, celiac serology and CRP today. She would like to see GI regardless of results to sort out the bowel piece; referral placed. Will message results.

documents.title: Results From Monday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Julie, everything from Monday is normal: no anemia, iron stores fine, thyroid normal, celiac test negative, inflammation marker normal, kidney and liver tests fine. Reassuring. Keep the GI appointment.

documents.title: RE: Results From Monday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good to hear. GI could fit me in December 16th, so I took it.

medications.drug: polyethylene glycol 3350 17000 MG Powder for Oral Solution

medications.reason: irritable bowel syndrome with constipation spells

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the GI visit from 12/16. We have no letter yet; history from Julie.

She says the gastroenterologist examined her, reviewed our November labs, and called it irritable bowel syndrome, the mixed type. Started her on polyethylene glycol powder, one capful in a drink on days she is backed up. Using it maybe twice a week. Some diet suggestions. Bloating a little better.

The bigger piece today is stress. This year she took on extra duties at school on top of her classes and has been anxious most days since early fall, lying awake running through to-do lists, waking at 4. She thinks the tiredness and the gut flares follow the bad weeks. No panic attacks. Not depressed, still enjoys weekends. No thoughts of self-harm. No substance use.

GAD-7 9, PHQ-9 6.

Exam: BP and weight stable. Appears a little tense, linear and engaged. Abdomen soft, nontender.

Assessment:
1. IBS, mixed, newly diagnosed by GI. PEG as needed added to her list per report.
2. Situational anxiety with sleep disruption, tied to the job change.

Plan: Talked through sleep habits, a fixed wind-down, caffeine before noon only. Offered a counseling referral; she would rather try on her own first and will tell me if it is not improving. No medication. Our staff will request the GI consult note. Check in by video in about three months.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Called the outside GI office for the 12/16/24 consult note. They show it signed but never sent to us. Request faxed with patient's release; they said 1 to 2 weeks.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammography with tomosynthesis. Prior studies from 2022 and 2023 reviewed. Scattered fibroglandular tissue. No suspicious mass, calcification or distortion. Stable appearance.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1: negative. Return in one year.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY GROUP - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 12/16/2024
Referring: primary care
Reason: fatigue, bloating, change in bowel habit

Ms. Duffy is a 45-year-old teacher seen at the request of her primary care physician. For about half a year she has found ordinary days harder to get through: persistent tiredness, trouble thinking clearly, and bloating that comes and goes. Her stools swing between constipation and diarrhea; the amount passed is not changed. For several weeks she has felt full in the lower abdomen, a little better after a bowel movement, and needs to rest after light exertion. No meaningful weight loss, appetite largely preserved though she is not hungry first thing in the morning. She connects all of this to stress since her job responsibilities changed, and reports anxiety and poor sleep.

Past history: cesarean section at 32. No chronic illness.
Medications: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: maternal aunt with papillary thyroid cancer; father hypertension; mother osteoporosis.
Social: high school teacher, never smoker, no alcohol.

Examination: Abdomen mildly distended with slight tenderness across both lower quadrants. No palpable mass, no guarding or rebound.

Data: Laboratory testing from her PCP in November is normal, including CBC, metabolic panel, TSH, ferritin, celiac serology and CRP. FIT negative 9/2024.

Impression: Irritable bowel syndrome, mixed subtype, meeting symptom criteria, with no alarm features and normal laboratory evaluation. Stress and sleep disruption likely contributing.

Recommendations:
1. Polyethylene glycol 3350, 17 g in liquid once daily as needed for constipation.
2. Soluble fiber, regular meals, trial of a reduced fermentable carbohydrate diet with handout.
3. Address stress and sleep with her PCP.
4. No endoscopic evaluation needed at this time. Return as needed.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from her kitchen after school.

Anxiety: better. She dropped one of the extra committees and has kept the evening routine. Asleep by 10:30 most nights, still the odd early waking. GAD-7 5 today (9 in January). Does not want counseling or medicine.

IBS: fewer flares since cutting back on some trigger foods and adding fiber. Uses the PEG a few times a month. No bleeding, weight stable by her home scale.

Assessment: situational anxiety improving; IBS-M controlled.
Plan: continue current approach. Physical in August.

documents.title: Appointment Cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt cancelled 8/20 physical, pulled into building meetings before classes start. First opening that works with her schedule is the Friday school breaks for the holidays; booked 12/19 at 10:00. Flu/COVID to be done separately in October.

documents.title: Vaccine Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 2025-26 flu vaccine L deltoid and 2025-26 COVID vaccine R deltoid. No acute illness, temp normal. Fine after 15 minutes of observation. Reminded her of the December physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, moved from August. First day of break and she sounds relieved.

Interval: IBS quiet most weeks; PEG maybe twice a month. Gut flares still track with busy stretches. Stress much more manageable this fall, sleeping through most nights. No new symptoms. NKDA. Only PEG as needed.

GAD-7 4, PHQ-9 3.

Exam: Vitals and weight as charted, unchanged. HEENT clear. Neck supple, no cervical adenopathy. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. No edema. Calm, good eye contact.

A/P:
- Preventive: CBC, CMP, lipids today. Mammogram order for January. FIT is due again; new kit given. Pap/HPV due next year, will do at next physical. Vaccines current for the season.
- IBS, mixed: stable on PEG as needed.
- Situational anxiety: much improved, no treatment needed.
Next physical in about a year; reach me by message for anything sooner.

documents.title: Results From Your Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count, chemistry and cholesterol all look good. Enjoy the break. Don't forget the stool kit when you get a chance.

reports.text: Bilateral 3D screening mammogram. Compared with January 2025 and earlier. Breast tissue is scattered fibroglandular. No suspicious masses, calcifications or areas of distortion. No change.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1, negative. Next screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Reminder: Stool Test Kit
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Julie, our records show the colon screening kit you took home in December hasn't come back to the lab yet. If you've misplaced it, reply here and we'll mail a new one.

reports.text: Real-time ultrasound of the thyroid and central neck. Right lobe: a 2.0 cm solid hypoechoic nodule with irregular margins and punctate microcalcifications. Remainder of the right lobe, the isthmus and the left lobe are of normal size and homogeneous echotexture without other nodules. No abnormal-appearing cervical lymph nodes.
reports.conclusion: 2.0 cm solid, hypoechoic right thyroid nodule with irregular margins and microcalcifications, highly suspicious (ACR TI-RADS TR5). Fine-needle aspiration recommended.

documents.title: Endocrinology New Patient Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY - NEW PATIENT
Visit date: 03/02/2026
Self-referred. Copy to primary care physician.

Reason for visit: lump in the neck.

History: 46-year-old woman, a teacher, who found a lump low on the right side of her neck about a month ago while getting ready for work. It does not hurt. She has a feeling of fullness there and now and then food seems to catch on the way down. Her voice is unchanged, and she has noticed no change in weight, appetite or energy. Past history includes irritable bowel syndrome, worked up in December 2024 for fatigue and bloating. Cesarean section at 32.

Medications: polyethylene glycol 3350 17 g daily as needed.
Allergies: none known.
Family history: a maternal aunt had papillary thyroid cancer. Father with hypertension, mother with osteoporosis.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: Firm, non-tender nodule of about 2 cm in the right thyroid lobe, moves with swallowing. No cervical lymphadenopathy. Otherwise normal.

Labs today: TSH 2.5 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), free T4 1.2 ng/dL (0.8-1.8). Euthyroid.

Imaging: ultrasound in clinic today shows a 2 cm solid hypoechoic nodule in the right lobe with irregular margins and microcalcifications.

Assessment: right thyroid nodule with suspicious sonographic features for malignancy, normal thyroid function, family history of papillary thyroid cancer.

Plan: ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration next week; she is scheduled for 3/10. Results and next steps to follow.

documents.title: Your Endocrinology Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Julie, the endocrinology note from Monday came in. I'm sorry you've been dealing with this; you could have messaged me first, but it sounds like you're in good hands and the biopsy is the right next step. Let me know what it shows or if you want to talk anything through.

documents.title: RE: Your Endocrinology Visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. My aunt went through this so I just called them directly, didn't want to wait. Biopsy is Tuesday. I'll keep you posted.

documents.title: Pharmacy Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pharmacist called. Pt filled levothyroxine 112 mcg daily, calcitriol 0.25 mcg BID and calcium carbonate 1250 mg TID on 4/14, prescribed by a general surgeon. Pharmacist asked whether we wanted anything changed and wanted to be sure she knows to take the levothyroxine at least 4 hours apart from calcium. We had no record of surgery.

Called pt. She had a total thyroidectomy on 4/13 at a regional hospital, home the next day. Says the biopsy in March came back suspicious and the surgeon recommended taking the whole thyroid. She is taking levothyroxine first thing on an empty stomach and the calcium with meals; reviewed spacing. Post-op visit with surgery is 4/27. Some numbness around her mouth on and off since she got home; told her to call surgery today about that and to go to the ED for muscle spasms or cramping that won't stop. She agrees.

Records request (op note, pathology, discharge summary) faxed to the hospital. FYI to PCP.

documents.title: Update after surgery
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to update you. Saw the surgeon Monday. The tingling in my lips and fingers was my calcium being low, it was 7.0. They said the parathyroid glands aren't working right after the surgery and doubled the calcitriol to 0.5 twice a day, same calcium and same thyroid pill. Had blood drawn again today at their office. Pathology was papillary cancer, small, they said they got it all and the lymph nodes were clear. Endocrinology will manage everything from here. Still tired and my hands cramp sometimes but better than last week.

documents.title: RE: Update after surgery
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me, Julie, and I'm glad the nodes were clear. Low calcium after thyroid surgery is common, and following it closely with surgery and endocrinology is exactly right. If the cramping or tingling gets worse, or your hands or face start to spasm, go to the ED. We've asked the hospital for your operative and pathology reports. Rest up.

documents.title: General Surgery Postoperative Visit
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
GENERAL SURGERY - POSTOPERATIVE FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 04/27/2026

Indication and course: Right thyroid nodule, TR5 on ultrasound; FNA 03/10/2026 at an outside endocrinology office read as suspicious for papillary thyroid carcinoma. Total thyroidectomy 04/13/2026, uneventful in hospital, discharged 04/14 on levothyroxine 112 mcg daily, calcium carbonate 1250 mg three times daily with meals and calcitriol 0.25 mcg twice daily.

Pathology: papillary thyroid carcinoma, classic type, 1.9 cm, right lobe. Margins negative. No extrathyroidal extension. No lymphovascular invasion. Central lymph nodes 0/3.

Interval: Two weeks of worsening tiredness, occasional difficulty swallowing, and tingling around the lips and at the fingertips. Intermittent calf cramping. Her throat feels tight when she talks for a long stretch. Over the last three days it all gets worse when she is up and moving. Denies lightheadedness, palpitations, or any recent stomach bug.

Medications: levothyroxine 112 mcg daily; calcium carbonate 1250 mg TID with meals; calcitriol 0.25 mcg BID; polyethylene glycol 3350 17 g daily as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: noncontributory.
Social: teacher; never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: Mildly anxious. Incision healing well, no hematoma or seroma. Intermittent twitching of the hand muscles while she talks. Cranial nerves II-XII intact; strength full; occasional involuntary contraction of the hands.

Labs today: calcium 7.0 mg/dL, phosphate 5.6 mg/dL, magnesium 1.8 mEq/L.

Assessment: Postprocedural hypoparathyroidism after total thyroidectomy, symptomatic. Papillary thyroid carcinoma, low risk, resected.

Plan:
1. Calcitriol increased to 0.5 mcg twice daily. Continue calcium carbonate 1250 mg TID with meals and levothyroxine 112 mcg daily.
2. Repeat calcium at our office within the week.
3. Endocrinology to assume long-term management of calcium and thyroid hormone replacement.
4. Emergency evaluation for carpopedal spasm, worsening cramps, or throat tightness.
cc: primary care physician (sent on request)

documents.title: Records Status
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Surgery office faxed their 4/27 follow-up note after our second request; it includes the biopsy and pathology summary. Operative report and discharge summary still not received from the hospital. Scanned for PCP review.

documents.title: Endo visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update. Saw endocrinology last Monday. Calcium is back up to the low end of normal and they're keeping me on the same calcitriol, calcium and thyroid doses. Feeling a lot more like myself, no more tingling. Do I need to come in before school starts?

documents.title: RE: Endo visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news. No need to come in before September unless something changes. Could you ask the endocrinology office to send us their notes? We didn't get one from this visit. Your physical is due in December and we'll catch up on everything then.
